package_info.package_name: Unknown (malicious NPM package delivered via jsdelivr)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (package already removed from NPM registry, but still delivered via CDN)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because it was designed to harvest victims’ credentials and was distributed through both the NPM registry and the jsdelivr CDN, continuing to pose a threat even after removal from the official registry.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when the malicious package is loaded or executed in a project)
execution_context.file_location: main entry point of the malicious NPM package (e.g., index.js or main.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code accesses environment variables (potentially containing credentials), and sends their values to a hardcoded external domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting environment variables and exfiltrating them to an external server is a classic credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal NPM packages should not access sensitive environment variables or transmit them to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate telemetry or error reporting tools may send non-sensitive environment data for debugging, but never credentials.
key_indicators: Access to process.env or similar credential sources
Network requests to hardcoded, non-official domains
No user interaction or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User installs or loads the malicious NPM package, either directly or via jsdelivr CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in the victim's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, harvesting credentials from environment variables or local files.
Harvested credentials are exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials, enabling further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: NPM package code that reads environment variables or credential files at import-time or runtime
Outbound network requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains from package initialization code
Credential harvesting logic embedded in package entry points
file_indicators: NPM packages with obfuscated or minified code in index.js/main.js
References to process.env or fs.readFileSync for sensitive files
Packages loaded via jsdelivr CDN after removal from NPM registry
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate application
Connections to known malicious exfiltration endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for NPM packages (especially those loaded via CDN) that access environment variables or credential files and initiate outbound network connections at import-time or runtime. Flag packages that attempt to exfiltrate data to untrusted domains, and review any code that performs credential harvesting or network exfiltration in package entry points.
